A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Gaussian Atlas/GaussianVerse study. Their main text, equations, Tables 1–3, Figures 1–17, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original text-to-3D benchmark results, a pairwise user study, ablations, and appendix experiments on Gaussian fitting and VAE reconstruction.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark, user-study, ablation, and appendix results.

M1.justification: Sections 3–5 and Appendices A–C retain the same visibility-based pruning, optimal-transport atlas construction, VAE-free UNet fine-tuning, losses, and inference procedure. The wording edits do not change the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same GaussianVerse object data and zero-shot text-to-3D task. The appendix retains the same prompts, diversity examples, and long-prompt cases; no dataset, domain, or test scenario is added.

E2.justification: Table 2 and Figure 5 retain DreamGaussian, LGM, TriplaneGaussian, and GaussianCube. Appendix comparisons retain Scaffold-GS, GaussianCube, and Splatter Image. Newly cited TRELLIS and DiffSplat are not evaluated.

E3.justification: The reported protocol remains 100 test prompts, 10 random renderings, CLIP/VQA scoring, and over 2,500 user-study responses. Training settings are retained. The new relative training-budget statement documents an existing comparison rather than revising a previously stated setting.

E4.justification: Figures 8–10 retain the pretraining, flattening, and weight-difference analyses. Appendix fitting and VAE analyses, diversity examples, and long-prompt failures are also unchanged; no analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the Gaussian-count mean and standard deviation in Table 1. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative examples are unchanged, including the appendices. Table 2 retains GaussianAtlas at 23.20 CLIP/0.61 VQA and GaussianCube at 22.31/0.52; Figure 7 retains 65.4% and 88.0% preferences. The new 0.9-point CLIP and 17% relative VQA comparisons summarize existing values.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4 and the atlas-construction mathematics are unchanged. Shortening the explicit input-shape notation preserves the same two-dimensional requirement; no mathematical assumption, derivation, or proof is substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about GaussianVerse, Gaussian Atlas, repurposing pretrained 2D diffusion models, and improved generation alignment and user preference.

C2.justification: Section 6.1 newly frames the existing alignment results as achieved with half GaussianCube's 3D training steps. Section 2 removes the specific attribution of GIMDiffusion's seam artifacts to sparse UV maps. Appendix E's detail-versus-cost and long-prompt limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 6.1 newly states that the method uses half as many training steps on 3D data as GaussianCube, adding relative budget information for the existing comparison. The method's one-million-step, eight-A100 setup, appendix implementation details, and project access information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds TRELLIS and DiffSplat and revises the comparison with nearby 2D representations. The bibliography also replaces the mismatched reference attached to DiffGS with 'DiffGS: Functional Gaussian Splatting Diffusion.' These are limited literature and positioning updates.

P1.justification: v2 removes the duplicated user-study passage, adds a dedicated quantitative-results paragraph, lightly condenses method and results prose, and adds acknowledgments and an internship footnote. The overall section and appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: All figures and numbered tables are retained. There are small figure-size and spacing adjustments, a shortened Figure 9 caption, and text/figure reflow around the revised results section and acknowledgments. These changes do not introduce new visual evidence.

improvement.justification: Removing the duplicate user-study text and explaining Table 2 improve readability, while the added related work and corrected DiffGS reference improve scholarly accuracy. These resolve limited presentation and citation deficiencies; the scientific evidence and documented limitations remain unchanged.
